Params: Karenina leaves the "happy room" behind, but she still has not made it back to reality.
The explosions keep going, rolling inward from the edges and consuming everything in their paths.
Karenina sees a computer tangled in countless cables. Its name goes without saying.
This is Carcosa's chamber. Or rather, its mental landscape.
Why, Karenina? Why destroy all of this? Wouldn't it be better to stay?
Isn't that what you wanted? The ultimate peace?
I should be asking you that, Carcosa. What kind of pretentious name is that anyway?
You didn't think a cheap illusion like this could trap me, did you?!
But... this illusion has trapped so many others.
If I still had my bombs, I'd blow this whole place to smithereens!
This pathetic illusion is not what I want!
They were just some twisted, warped versions of Grandpa, Wise, my friends, my comrades, and Commandant!
What do you think happiness is?
Since you don't know, why don't I tell you, you damn machine?!
Real happiness isn't some manufactured perfection! It's the imperfect reality I build with my own two hands, my beliefs, and the people I cherish!
If defining happiness through some rigid template could create perfection, then I'd be betraying myself, and—
Karenina places her hand over her heart.
My anchor isn't here. No matter what kind of picture you paint for me, it's not what I want.
You never believed in the Song of True Love?
Of course not! Why would I hand over the right to decide something I can figure out to you?!
What kind of person would I be if I lack that much faith in myself?!
Perhaps you truly are more unique than the others.
But you're still just one of them in the end.
No matter how enlightened you are, your fate was sealed the moment you arrived here.
Stay here. Your memories and you shall become part of Xoth and become my specimen.
Why refuse the will of a god?
I don't need a reason. No means no. I, Karenina, don't need handouts from anyone!
The future I want, the happiness I'm after... I'll create them with my own two hands! Got it?!
Unfortunately for you, I wield far greater power than anyone else here in Xoth.
Especially now that I'm about to be free of the lance that fate has bound me to.
Carcosa cheats, smothering Karenina in layer upon layer of data and crimson matter.
To devour instead of understand... that is the logic of the Punishing Virus, and it has become Carcosa's logic as well.
Dammit... I'm not giving up here!
Within the datastream, Karenina curls up, bracing for the next impact.
When she finally breaks free from these shackles, she knows that the moment she opens her eyes, you will be the first thing she sees.
Because someone's out there waiting for me!
Karenina doesn't know it yet, but the seashell in her hand is glowing, its light spreading like branches, wrapping around her.
It courses through her entire body, forming something like a protective membrane that shields her from outside corruption.
Then, Karenina's consciousness breaks free from Carcosa's gravity, plunging into the deep sea and slipping through the currents before returning to reality.
Outside her M.I.N.D., you are still chasing after Karenina.
Until she reaches the coffin and stops.
Karenina turns around and smiles at you.
Commandant... you idiot... you really are...
Unlike in the dream, though, Karenina winks at you.
Her expression goes blank again as she lowers herself into the coffin.
You throw off your restraints and block the coffin lid, refusing to let them close it.
The Choir members surge forward, but they hesitate, fearing you might do something even more reckless.
Our Great One has awakened. The Song of True Love has reached the depths of chaos.
The Songstress is restoring the King in Yellow. No mortal fool shall interrupt.
I won't let you take Karenina.
You pull out a detonator and expose the fuse. The Choir members freeze, terrified you will do something even crazier.
The Administrator waves everyone back and returns to a composed tone.
Of course. The Choir acknowledges the bond you share.
No one is taking Karenina from you. She'll wake up once the departure ceremony concludes.
There's no need to be nervous. You can see for yourself that she's fine. The ceremony has already begun.
Don't let all our efforts go to waste here.
Let me see her one more time.
If the Song of True Love really did awaken something...
Then I should be with Karenina.
Here or in outer space... wherever she goes.
The Administrator glances at Karenina. Seeing how peacefully she is lying there, the Administrator finally approves.
Karenina has never looked so still. She lies there like flowers and candles arranged before an altar.
She is becoming a Songstress for Carcosa and Xoth... if nothing goes wrong, that is.
Suppressing your grief and rage temporarily, you lean against the cold wood and carefully place the detonator on her.
Amid the chanting and howling winds, you lean down, as if to kiss your lover one last time.
Only at this distance can you avoid everyone's watchful eyes.
Just as you are about to make contact with Karenina, she blows away a strand of hair that has fallen across her face.
At this intimate distance, she murmurs a complaint so quietly that only the two of you can hear.
You took your sweet time getting here, Commandant.
Any later and I would have blown this place up myself.
Only now can you finally breathe a sigh of relief.
It is Karenina. If you can't confirm her safety with your own eyes, there's no telling where this story will lead.
I'm ready. Let's stick to the plan.
Karenina nods, keeping her eyes closed, though her lashes won't stop trembling because of the trapped air between you.
Carcosa glances dismissively at you two, unaware that through its gifted "happiness"...
Karenina's consciousness has already returned from that stranded world.
What remains in its mental prison is nothing more than a false body conjured from a seashell.
A crucial prop must be used at the crucial moment. The captain, well-versed in the ways of story, laid the groundwork for this twist from the very beginning.
Of course, to an outside observer, your "kiss" is lasting a bit too long.
Separate them. It's time to set sail.
The moment you are dragged away, the coffin lid slams shut.
Before Carcosa's words even finish, the anchor, now wired to detonators, bursts through the coffin and strikes Carcosa dead-on.
The instant the explosion goes off, you grab Karenina's hand and leap, dodging the barrage of strikes behind you and climbing your way onto the fallen deity's back.
Seemingly realizing your true intention, Carcosa pivots to ram itself into the coastal rocks, attempting to snap the lance on its back.

Thrown off by the impact, you feel a wave of scorching heat slamming into your face. You whip around, only to find yourself staring into a gaping, bloodied maw, where rows upon rows of fangs writhe inside.
The lance is about to break.
I believe in Kiki. We just need to buy her a little more time. She'll get the CPF back online.
You can be a real pain to deal with if you want, so Carcosa won't shake you off that easily. All you need to do is keep it busy long enough to buy Kiki more time.
You grip onto the fangs, restraining the Great One like a festering wound that refuses to heal.
In the split second the lance snaps, it vanishes completely from everyone's sight.
As Carcosa breaks free and spreads all its appendages to devour you, Karenina and you clasp hands, bracing against the sweltering wind to keep yourselves from falling.
Just as the strike closes in, Carcosa freezes mid-motion, and the lance on its back respawns.
The newly restored weapon rises from the depths, pinning the fallen deity in place.
The CPF's back online! She did it!
The night before, Karenina informed Kiki of the real location of the CPF.
Kiki went there alone to repair it. Despite her self-doubt, she accepted this extra test.
Sensing its demise is inevitable, Carcosa unleashes a feral shriek and one final, desperate attack.
It opens its maw wide, hoping to devour the intruders. Before the shadow of its mouth falls over you, you shove Karenina out of the way.
Inside its sweltering maw, you fight back waves of nausea, grabbing the tip of the lance and striking downward with all your strength.
Sloosh! The damage spreads, and the fallen deity secretes more viscous fluid. You nearly lose your footing.
The wounded Carcosa thrashes its head violently, trying to either swallow you whole or shake you loose.
But the helter-skelter impact is brought to a halt.
You still with me?! Just hang on a little longer!
I've hooked this monster's head with the anchor! It won't take long, Commandant!
You steady yourself in the darkness, shifting your weight to keep balance. It is almost over—Karenina is fighting alongside you out there.
The fallen deity's life drains away completely, and it sinks into the depths. You finally let yourself collapse.
Until you feel the dead thing carrying you hits the ocean floor and stirs up clouds of sediment.
Until someone pries open its fangs... Even her silhouette looks lively.
She enters your vision bathed in light.
Commandant! Thank god you're okay. Let's get out of here!
You take her hand and let her help you off the battlefield.
The struggle earlier has taken you both a good distance away. Lying behind you, Carcosa is nothing but a heap of useless scrap metal now.
Supported by Karenina, you stand on higher ground and watch Xoth's projection fade in the distance. The crowd erupts into chaos.
Every silhouette dissolves into blue, jellyfish-like bubbles, swelling, rising, and bursting one by one.
When truth is revealed, lies naturally fade away.
Is it really over? You look at each other, and Karenina, covered in grime, grins without a care in the world.
First thing I'm going to do when we get back is to take a nice long bath. This is a brand new frame, dammit!
And don't you laugh, Commandant! You don't look any better right now!
You can't help but smile as well. Yeah... it is finally over.
Comms are back! Come on, let's get Kiki!
But hurry up! If we leave now, she might still make it in time for the evaluation!
That's the Engineering Force, I guess.
